question: Should OpenClaw adopt this new repository-wide localization runtime, command-localization protocol field, and fail-closed readiness gate as a core product direction, or should the proposal be narrowed to existing surface-owned localization seams?
rationale: The proposed API and release-governance boundary affect multiple owners and plugins; code review cannot determine whether that permanent product contract is desired.

options.title: Approve and stage the architecture
options.body: Sponsor the shared runtime and protocol direction, then require rebased, independently landable slices with compatibility and live behavior proof.

options.title: Narrow to existing localization surfaces
options.body: Keep localization ownership within existing UI, CLI, and channel seams and remove the new cross-product protocol and release-gate contract.

options.title: Pause pending RFC decision
options.body: Leave the draft open only as RFC implementation material until the linked localization RFC receives an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Approve and stage the architecture
recommendation.body: Sponsor the shared runtime and protocol direction, then require rebased, independently landable slices with compatibility and live behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked RFC and all five commits in the submitted localization series, making them the clearest contact to supply or relay the requested decision context.
